title: Industry Pulse - AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: ITEM (y) FIRED ON ITS FIRST WORKING DAY - xAI shipped Grok 4.7 yesterday as 'its most capable model yet for coding and agents', a TRUE sentence about xAI's own lineup that implies a false thing about the frontier, and the independent measurement puts it at 26% on agentic coding against 55% for the model we already run
bullets.summary: IN WINDOW - dateline read at the page, published 2026-09-21T16:56Z, the first genuinely in-window item in five fires. Archive grep across 85 files: 'Grok 4.7' ZERO, AA-Briefcase ZERO, 'Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index' ZERO, 'Harvey Legal' ZERO, HealthBench ZERO, 'parametric CAD' ZERO - while bare 'Grok' sits in 22 files. Grok 4.7 is a larger base model with a longer RL run, priced at $2/M input and $6/M output, 'closer to Chinese models than Western frontier models, probably for good reason.' On the independent Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.3.2 it scores 46 and lands mid-pack; Claude Fable 5.1 and GPT-6 lead at 53 each. On Terminal-Bench 4.0 agentic coding - the benchmark closest to what The Construct does all day - Grok 4.7 scores 26%, against GPT-6 Astra at 60% and Claude Fable 5.1 at 55%; even the cheaper DeepSeek V4.1 Flash edges past it at 27%. LABELLED UNDER (w): the vendor-side agentic numbers (AA-Briefcase +111 Elo to 1657, Harvey Legal 15.8->19.6%, HealthBench Professional 48.5->56.7%, EEBench 53.0->64.0%, 500K context, agentic evals on parametric CAD and electrical/chip design) were read only in secondary summary and are reported as xAI's claims, not as measurements this report verified.
bullets.how: (i) NO SWITCH on our main workload - our agentic-coding surface is Claude Code and the measured gap is 26% against 55%; price does not buy that back. (ii) The one lane worth a bookmark is VironBox/STRUCTA: xAI claims training on agentic parametric CAD and electrical/chip design, the only place in the estate where a cheap mid-pack model could beat a frontier model never trained on the task. That is a test, not an adoption. (iii) THE REAL FINDING IS METHODOLOGICAL. Three secondaries carried the vendor framing verbatim; each sentence is true within xAI's lineup and false about the frontier. Yesterday's (y) test was written for 'first' and generalises without modification to 'best', 'most capable' and 'state of the art': name the comparison set, then ask who is outside it.

bullets.title: A hard deadline in two days this report has never written down: the Sora 2 API is deleted on 24 September, every call returns 410 Gone, the replacement column is empty, and all Sora account data is destroyed with no recovery window
bullets.summary: DECLARED AS A DEADLINE, NOT NEWS - the deprecation was notified 24 March 2026, 182 days ago. Archive grep across 85 files: 'Sora' appears in exactly 2 files (14 Jul, 15 Sep) and in BOTH it is a bare model name inside an aggregator's list of what a video connector routes to; the shutdown date, the 410 and the data deletion are ZERO. Read at the vendor primary: this was always a two-stage shutdown - the consumer app and web experience died 26 April 2026; the Videos API and every sora-2 / sora-2-pro alias and dated snapshot are removed 24 September 2026; the recommended-replacement column for that row is EMPTY, because OpenAI has no video model to move to. Alternatives named in the current market for when we repoint: Veo 3.1, Kling 3.0, Runway Gen-4.5, Seedance 2.5.
bullets.how: (i) VERIFIED NEGATIVE ON OUR SIDE, and this report almost never gets to state one: a grep of the entire 126-skill estate returns ZERO references to sora, sora-2 or sora2. Nothing we author names the dying alias. (ii) THE UNVERIFIED HALF IS THE VENDOR'S - our video generation runs through a third-party creative connector that routes to a pool of models, and both archive mentions of Sora are exactly that. Exposure is not 'none', it is 'none that we author, unknown that we rent.' The fifteen-minute job before Thursday is to ask the connector which models it routes and confirm it has repointed. (iii) THE STRUCTURAL LESSON IS ABOUT RENTED CAPABILITY: a capability we never wrote, never configured and cannot enumerate can still be deleted on a date we were told about in March - item (k) pointed outward instead of inward.

bullets.title: ARCHIVE MISS, 187 days old and ZERO across 85 files - somebody measured a public skill registry and found more than 30% of 26,502 skills carry a suspicious or malicious flag, that risk concentrates in exactly the functions our estate is built on, and that the biggest risk contributors are organisations acting in good faith
bullets.summary: Dateline read at the primary: arXiv:2604.13064v1 [cs.CL], 19 Mar 2026. Archive grep across 85 files: ClawHub ZERO, 2604.13064 ZERO, '26,502' ZERO, AUROC ZERO, 'submission-time' ZERO; 'Red Skills' appears in 4 files but every hit is OUR OWN internal red/blue vocabulary, not this paper. A normalised corpus of 26,502 skills crawled to 18 Mar 2026: more than 30% flagged suspicious or malicious by platform signals, and the proportion has NOT declined as the registry grew, while the count labelled neither safe nor suspicious stays persistently high. Of 9,000+ suspicious skills only ~600 carry a fine-grained label across seven categories, four with fewer than 100 samples. Risk concentrates BY FUNCTION, not by author intent: skills that execute code, make outbound network/API calls, or process multimedia are disproportionately risky. And the finding that should sting - the top-15 contributors of risky skills are largely companies acting in good faith; the risk comes from the complexity and usage scenario of their skills, and a skill benign at upload can have its vulnerability discovered later. Submission-time risk prediction on 11,010 balanced samples: best Logistic Regression 72.62% accuracy / 78.95% AUC, within 8 points of an LLM-based classifier; the primary documentation is the single most informative feature, and dropping the summary IMPROVES accuracy, because risky skills use harmless-looking summaries to mislead.
bullets.how: (i) CORRECTION TO YESTERDAY'S OWN NUMBER: the estate is 126 skills, not 125. (ii) The paper's risk-concentrating functions ARE our estate - execute code, call outbound APIs, process media: b9-site-repair-headless, hermes-worker-queue, b9-site-deploy, higgsfield-browser-studio, vironbox-render-node, ans-engine-autonomy. Not a fringe of the corpus, its spine - and item (k) is still not run on its 24th day. (iii) 'RISK FROM COMPLEXITY, NOT MALICE' kills the implicit defence 'our skills are ours, so they're fine.' (iv) ITEM (t) GAINS A THIRD COLUMN AND IT IS FREE: capability class - executes code / calls out / handles media - because that is the column the measurement says predicts risk. (v) A METHOD WE CAN COPY VERBATIM: score on the primary documentation, distrust the summary. Our 126 SKILL.md files are exactly 'primary documentation plus a summary', so this is a testable claim about our own corpus needing no vendor and no budget.

bullets.how: One rule generalised on its first working day ((y)), one new rule opened on a real failure ((z)), one method failure declared rather than hidden (the Claude Code primary), one verified negative reported (Sora across 126 skills), and one standing-list test FAILED honestly ((p)).

praxis_lesson: The first genuinely in-window item in five fires arrived with a vendor sentence attached - 'its most capable model yet for coding, agents, and knowledge work' - and the sentence is TRUE. It is true about xAI's own lineup and it implies something false about the frontier, where the independent index reads 46 against 53 and agentic coding reads 26% against 55%. Item (y) was written yesterday for the word 'first'; it fired today on the word 'best', and the generalisation is the day's real output: NAME THE COMPARISON SET, THEN ASK WHO IS OUTSIDE IT. SECOND, AND IT CUTS THE OTHER WAY: the grep that protects this report from repeating itself nearly deleted the day's most applicable finding. 'Red Skills' returned four archive hits and all four were our own internal vocabulary, not the 26,502-skill registry measurement that has sat unread for 187 days. A MATCHING STRING IS NOT COVERAGE - when a grep hits, read the hit. That is new item (z), and it is the mirror image of (y): (y) stops a true sentence implying too much, (z) stops a true match implying too much. THIRD, THE ACTION, THE SAME LINE FOR THE FOURTH CONSECUTIVE DAY BUT NOW WITH A COLUMN THAT MAKES IT TRACTABLE: cut the [B] leg off the research jobs and audit what the push credentials reach - and enumerate the 126 skills BY CAPABILITY CLASS, because the measurement says risk is predicted by what a skill can do, not by who wrote it or whether they meant well. Every skill in this estate was written in good faith. The paper's finding is that good faith is not the variable. FOURTH, THE ONE CLEAN WIN: a grep of all 126 skills for the Sora aliases that die on Thursday returned ZERO. This report is allowed to report a verified negative, and it should, because the same grep exposed the shape of the real exposure - nothing we author names the dying model, but our video capability is RENTED from a connector whose routing we cannot enumerate. A capability nobody here configured can still be deleted on a date we were told about in March. FIFTH, THE METHOD FAILURE, DECLARED RATHER THAN PAPERED OVER: the Claude Code changelog primary exceeded the reader's size cap and was not read at the page today, breaking an eight-day streak. The version is reported from secondaries and labelled as such. A streak is worth less than the admission that it ended.
